message.content:
I'm building a pharmacovigilance case processing backend. Spring Boot 3.2.x, 
Java 17, Maven. The project is already scaffolded at /backend with a working 
pom.xml and mvn spring-boot:run works.

Domain context: AI extracts structured fields from medical documents. Each field 
has a value, confidence score (0.0-1.0), and source reference like "p.4 §1". 
When a follow-up document arrives, we merge it with the stored case and annotate 
each field with a status: unchanged, overridden, new, or retained. Overridden 
fields also carry the previous value.

Full package structure we'll build across multiple steps:
  com.pv.cases.model        - CaseDocument, FieldValue, MergedCase, Query
  com.pv.cases.repository   - InMemoryCaseStore
  com.pv.cases.service      - MergeService, CaseService, QueryService
  com.pv.cases.controller   - CaseController, QueryController
  com.pv.cases.exception    - CaseNotFoundException, GlobalExceptionHandler
  com.pv.cases.config       - StartupDataLoader

RIGHT NOW, only plan the model classes. List each class, its fields with types, 
and any Jackson annotations you'd use. Do not write any code yet. Just the plan.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
Before the plan, two things I verified in the scaffold that change the answer:

**The stack isn't what you described.** `backend/pom.xml` is on `spring-boot-starter-parent:4.1.0`, not 3.2.x (Java 17 is correct). The starters are the Boot 4 reorganized ones — `spring-boot-starter-webmvc`, `spring-boot-starter-validation-test` — which is why they look wrong but resolve fine.

**That means Jackson 3, not Jackson 2.** Pulled in transitively via `spring-boot-starter-jackson`:
- `tools.jackson.databind` / `tools.jackson.core` @ 3.1.4 — note the `tools.*` root package
- annotations stayed put: `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.*` @ 2.21, so every `@JsonProperty`/`@JsonValue`/`@JsonCreator` import below is unchanged from what you'd expect
- `java.time` support is folded into databind (`tools.jackson.databind.ext.javatime`) — no `jackson-datatype-jsr310` dependency needed for `Instant`

Everything below assumes that. Also: `backend/.mvn/wrapper/` is missing, so `./mvnw` fails — use system `mvn` (which is presumably what's been working for you).

---

# Model class plan — `com.pv.cases.model`

## Cross-cutting decisions

**Records, not classes.** Java 17 + Jackson 3 deserializes records via their canonical constructor with no `@JsonCreator` needed. Merging is naturally a "produce a new value" operation, so immutability costs nothing here.

**`sections` stays a nested `Map`, not typed classes.** In `case_v1.json`, `patient`/`suspect_drug` and `weight_kg`/`event_term` are *data*, not schema — an AI extractor will invent sections and fields you didn't compile in. A `Map<String, Map<String, FieldValue>>` absorbs that, and it makes `MergeService` a generic two-level map walk instead of 20 hand-written field comparisons. Cost: no compile-time field safety and no per-field bean validation. I think that's the right trade for an extraction pipeline; say so if you'd rather have typed sections.

**snake_case via explicit `@JsonProperty`, not a global naming strategy.** `spring.jackson.property-naming-strategy=SNAKE_CASE` is one line and would work, but it only applies to the Boot-configured mapper — any `new ObjectMapper()` in a `MergeService` unit test silently produces different JSON. Per-component annotations travel with the type. Note this only affects the ~6 multi-word *properties*; map keys like `weight_kg` are never touched by either mechanism.

---

## 1. `FieldValue`

One extracted field as it comes off the AI. Record.

| Component | Type | Jackson |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | none needed |
| `confidence` | `Double` | none needed |
| `source` | `String` | none needed |

**No Jackson annotations at all** — all three names are already single lowercase words matching the JSON.

Two calls worth flagging:
- `Double`, not `double`. With a primitive, a missing `confidence` in a follow-up doc deserializes to `0.0`, which is indistinguishable from a real "the model had zero confidence" — and your merge rules will likely branch on confidence. Boxed + `@NotNull` makes absence detectable.
- `value` stays `String`. The seed file encodes everything as a string, including `"62"` and `"2026-03-12"`. Uniform typing keeps `equals()`-based change detection trivial. If you later need numeric comparison, that's a parse at the service layer, not a model change.

Validation (`spring-boot-starter-validation` is on the classpath): `@NotBlank` on `value`, `@NotNull @DecimalMin("0.0") @DecimalMax("1.0")` on `confidence`.

---

## 2. `CaseDocument`

One extracted version of a case — mirrors `case_v1.json` exactly. Record.

| Component | Type | Jackson |
|---|---|---|
| `caseId` | `String` | `@JsonProperty("case_id")` |
| `version` | `int` | none |
| `caseClassification` | `String` | `@JsonProperty("case_classification")` |
| `extractedAt` | `Instant` | `@JsonProperty("extracted_at")` |
| `sourceDocument` | `String` | `@JsonProperty("source_document")` |
| `sections` | `Map<String, Map<String, FieldValue>>` | none |

Class-level: `@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)`.

- `Instant` parses `"2026-04-08T09:14:00Z"` natively, and Boot disables `WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS`, so it round-trips as the same ISO string.
- `caseClassification` as `String` rather than an enum, deliberately. `"non-significant"` is a controlled vocabulary and an enum is tempting, but an unrecognized value in an inbound follow-up would then fail the whole deserialization instead of flowing through to a validation error you control. Worth revisiting once you know the full vocabulary.
- Use a `LinkedHashMap` when constructing so section/field order matches the source document — Jackson preserves insertion order on serialization, and a stable field order matters a lot when a reviewer is diffing two versions on screen.
- Bean-validation gotcha: cascading into nested maps needs container-element syntax — `Map<String, @Valid Map<String, @Valid FieldValue>>`. A plain `@Valid` on the field validates nothing inside.

---

## 3. `MergedField` — *addition to your list*

Your spec ("annotate each field with a status... overridden fields also carry the previous value") needs a type that isn't in your package listing. I'd keep it separate from `FieldValue` rather than adding nullable `status`/`previousValue` onto it — otherwise every inbound extraction carries two fields that are meaningless on input.

| Component | Type | Jackson |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `String` | none |
| `confidence` | `Double` | none |
| `source` | `String` | none |
| `status` | `FieldStatus` | none |
| `previousValue` | `FieldValue` | `@JsonProperty("previous_value")`, null unless `OVERRIDDEN` |

Class-level `@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)` so `previous_value` is simply absent on the other three statuses.

The value/confidence/source triple is **spelled out flat rather than composing a `FieldValue`**. Composition plus `@JsonUnwrapped` would be the tidier Java, but `@JsonUnwrapped` is not supported on creator parameters — it serializes fine and then fails to deserialize, which surfaces as a broken round-trip test rather than a compile error. Three duplicated components is the cheaper price.

---

## 4. `FieldStatus`

Standalone enum: `UNCHANGED, OVERRIDDEN, NEW, RETAINED`.

Your wire vocabulary is lowercase, Jackson's default enum output is the constant name. Rather than the global `WRITE_ENUMS_USING_TO_STRING` (same test-mapper divergence problem as above), give the enum a `String wireName` field with:
- `@JsonValue` on its accessor → serializes as `"overridden"`
- `@JsonCreator` on a static lookup → accepts `"overridden"` inbound, and lets you throw a clear error on an unknown token

Both annotations are `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.*`. Semantics to pin down now, since `MergeService` depends on them: **new** = key absent in stored, present in incoming; **overridden** = present in both, value differs; **unchanged** = present in both, value identical; **retained** = present in stored, absent from incoming. Open question for the merge step: does "differs" mean value-only, or value-or-confidence-or-source? I'd say value-only drives status, with confidence/source silently refreshed — otherwise a re-extraction that nudges confidence 0.94 → 0.95 floods the reviewer with false "overridden" flags.

---

## 5. `MergedCase`

The merge result — response-only, never deserialized from an extractor. Record.

| Component | Type | Jackson |
|---|---|---|
| `caseId` | `String` | `@JsonProperty("case_id")` |
| `version` | `int` | resulting version |
| `baseVersion` | `int` | `@JsonProperty("base_version")` |
| `incomingVersion` | `int` | `@JsonProperty("incoming_version")` |
| `caseClassification` | `String` | `@JsonProperty("case_classification")` |
| `mergedAt` | `Instant` | `@JsonProperty("merged_at")` |
| `sourceDocuments` | `List<String>` | `@JsonProperty("source_documents")` — accumulated provenance |
| `sections` | `Map<String, Map<String, MergedField>>` | none |
| `summary` | `MergeSummary` | none |

`sourceDocuments` as a list rather than a single `source_document`: in PV, "which document did this case state come from" is an audit question, and after two merges the answer is plural.

**`MergeSummary`** (nested record inside `MergedCase`): `int unchanged, overridden, added, retained` — note `added` as the Java component name since `new` is a reserved word, with `@JsonProperty("new")` to keep the wire vocabulary consistent with `FieldStatus`. This is a small thing that will bite whoever writes it if it isn't decided up front. It's pure derived data, but a reviewer UI wants "3 fields changed" without walking the map.

---

## 6. `Query` — needs your input

This is the one place your brief doesn't constrain the shape, and the two readings produce quite different classes. My assumption is **(a)**, but say the word if it's (b) and I'll re-plan just this piece.

**(a) Ask a question about a stored case** — fits the confidence/provenance theme, and makes `QueryService` the thing that answers "what was the onset date?" with a citation.

- `Query` (request): `caseId` (`String`, or bind from the path instead), `question` (`String`, `@NotBlank`), optional `sections` (`List<String>`) to scope the lookup
- plus a `QueryAnswer` response record: `question`, `answer` (`String`), `citations` (`List<FieldReference>` — section, field, value, confidence, source), `confidence` (`Double`, aggregate)

**(b) Search/filter across the case store** — `Query` becomes criteria: `caseClassification`, `minConfidence`, `field`, `hasStatus` (`FieldStatus`), `page`/`size`, wrapped in a `QueryResult<T>` page envelope. Choose this if `QueryController` is really a list endpoint.

---

Net: **6 new types** (`FieldValue`, `CaseDocument`, `MergedField`, `FieldStatus`, `MergedCase` + nested `MergeSummary`, `Query`) against the 4 in your outline — `MergedField` and `FieldStatus` fall out of the status-annotation requirement, and `MergeSummary` is optional if you'd rather the frontend count.

Two things to confirm before I write any of it: the `Query` reading above, and whether you want typed section classes instead of the open `Map`.

- Double not double for confidence ✓

content.text:
All six files created and verified. `mvn -o compile` is clean, and I ran the models against the real `case_v1.json` plus a synthetic follow-up.

## Verified behavior

Deserializing the seed file and re-serializing it reproduces the source shape — `case_id`, `extracted_at`, `source_document` all round-trip, `Instant` stays `"2026-04-08T09:14:00Z"`, and section/field order is preserved (`[initials, age, sex, weight_kg]`). Notably this was with a **bare `JsonMapper`**, no Spring config — which is exactly the property the per-field `@JsonProperty` decision was buying.

Merge output:
```json
{"value":"63","confidence":0.95,"source":"p.1 §2","status":"overridden",
 "previous_value":{"value":"62","confidence":0.91,"source":"p.2 §1"}}
```
`FieldStatus` emits `["unchanged","overridden","new","retained"]` and parses back; `MergeSummary` serializes `added` as `"new"`.

Bean validation cascades two map levels deep — a bad field surfaces as `sections[patient].<map value>[age].confidence`, so the nested `@Valid` syntax I flagged as a gotcha does work.

## Three things to know

**`missingFields` had to go on `CaseDocument` too, not just `MergedCase`.** You described `missing_fields` as arriving on the follow-up payload — and the follow-up payload deserializes into `CaseDocument`. Since Spring Boot disables `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES`, without the component the array would have been silently dropped before `MergeService` ever saw it, and there'd be nothing to surface. Verified it binds: `followup missingFields=[adverse_event.onset_date]`.

**`previousValue` was already `FieldValue` in the plan** — no change needed, it's the full field with confidence and source.

**Two additions beyond the plan**, both to protect `MergeService`, tell me if you'd rather they weren't there:
- Defensive copies in the compact constructors of `CaseDocument`/`MergedCase`. `InMemoryCaseStore` will hand the same instance to every caller, so this stops a merge from mutating the stored case in place. Confirmed: `sections` is unmodifiable. Uses `LinkedHashMap` + `unmodifiableMap` rather than `Map.copyOf`, whose iteration order is unspecified — that would have destroyed the field ordering.
- Four static factories on `MergedField` (`unchanged`/`overridden`/`added`/`retained`) plus a constructor guard rejecting `previousValue` on any non-`OVERRIDDEN` status. Makes the merge logic read as intent and the invariant unbreakable.

`Query.create(...)` generates the UUID and `createdAt`; `id`/`createdAt` are deliberately unvalidated so the same record can bind an inbound body that omits them. `sectionName()`/`fieldName()` split the path for the store lookup, and `field_path` is `@Pattern`-guarded to the two-level shape.

Unrelated, and worth a cleanup before this grows: **`backend/target/` is tracked in git** (from the scaffold commit), so build output shows up in every diff. Also `backend/.mvn/wrapper/` is missing, so `./mvnw` fails — only system `mvn` works. Say the word and I'll fix both.

Ready for the repository and `MergeService` layer whenever you are.

# Persistence & Startup Layer

## Context

The model layer (`com.pv.cases.model`) is committed at `2af083e`. The service has nowhere to
put a case and no data at boot, which blocks every layer above it. This step adds the
in-memory store and the startup seeder that loads `case_v1.json` into it, so that
`MergeService` / `CaseService` have something to read in the next step.

Nothing here is a service or controller — that stays out of scope by request.

## Binding constraint discovered during research: this is Jackson 3, not Jackson 2

Boot 4.1.0's `JacksonAutoConfiguration` (`org.springframework.boot.jackson.autoconfigure`)
declares exactly one mapper bean:

```
tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper jacksonJsonMapper(JsonMapper.Builder)
```

There is **no `ObjectMapper` bean method**. Injecting `ObjectMapper` still works, because
`JsonMapper extends tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper` (verified via `javap`) and Spring
resolves by assignable type. Three consequences that drive the code below:

1. The import must be **`tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper`**. `com.fasterxml.jackson.databind`
   is not on the classpath at all — only `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation` (2.21) is. The
   habitual import fails to compile, which is at least a loud failure rather than a silent one.
2. `readValue(InputStream, Class<T>)` throws **`tools.jackson.core.JacksonException`, which
   extends `RuntimeException`** — not a checked `IOException`. A `catch (IOException)` around
   the parse alone would be a compile error ("never thrown in body").
3. `IOException` is still reachable, but only from try-with-resources `close()`. So the catch
   clause must be `catch (IOException | JacksonException e)` — one for the stream, one for the parse.

`org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner` is unmoved in Boot 4.

## File 1 — `backend/src/main/java/com/pv/cases/repository/InMemoryCaseStore.java`

`@Repository`, two `ConcurrentHashMap` fields and the six methods as specified. Two
thread-safety details worth getting right, since the maps were specified as concurrent:

- **`queries` values must be `CopyOnWriteArrayList`, not `ArrayList`.** A `ConcurrentHashMap`
  makes the *map* safe; a plain `ArrayList` value would still corrupt under two concurrent
  `saveQuery` calls for the same case. Read-heavy query lists are the exact `CopyOnWriteArrayList`
  use case. Insert via `computeIfAbsent(...).add(query)`, which is atomic on `ConcurrentHashMap`.
- **`findQueriesByCaseId` returns `List.copyOf(...)`,** not the live list — consistent with the
  defensive copying already in `CaseDocument`/`MergedCase`, and it keeps callers from mutating
  stored state through the returned reference.

| Method | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `saveCase(String, CaseDocument)` | `cases.put(caseId, doc)` |
| `findCase(String)` | `Optional.ofNullable(cases.get(caseId))` |
| `saveQuery(Query)` | `queries.computeIfAbsent(query.caseId(), k -> new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>()).add(query)` |
| `findQueriesByCaseId(String)` | `List.copyOf(queries.getOrDefault(caseId, List.of()))` — empty list, never null |
| `caseCount()` | `cases.size()` |
| `queryCount()` | `queries.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum()` |

`saveQuery` keys off `query.caseId()`, so it rejects a null `caseId` with a clear
`NullPointerException` from `computeIfAbsent` rather than storing an unreachable entry.

## File 2 — `backend/src/main/java/com/pv/cases/config/StartupDataLoader.java`

`@Component implements ApplicationRunner`, constructor injection of `InMemoryCaseStore` and
`ObjectMapper`, SLF4J `Logger` via `LoggerFactory.getLogger(StartupDataLoader.class)`.

`run(ApplicationArguments args)`:

1. `InputStream in = getClass().getResourceAsStream("/case_v1.json")` as specified.
2. Null stream → `IllegalStateException("case_v1.json not found on the classpath; the case store would start empty")`.
3. `try (in) { doc = objectMapper.readValue(in, CaseDocument.class); }` — Java 9+ allows an
   effectively-final existing resource, so the null check stays outside the try.
   `catch (IOException | JacksonException e)` → rethrow as `IllegalStateException` naming the
   resource, with `e` as the cause.
4. **Case ID (per your decision):** assert the seed file matches, then key off the document.
   ```java
   private static final String EXPECTED_CASE_ID = "PV-2026-0451";
   ...
   if (!EXPECTED_CASE_ID.equals(doc.caseId())) {
       throw new IllegalStateException(
           "Expected seed case " + EXPECTED_CASE_ID + " but case_v1.json declares " + doc.caseId());
   }
   store.saveCase(doc.caseId(), doc);
   ```
5. Guard `doc.sections()` being null before `.size()` — `CaseDocument` deliberately preserves a
   null `sections` so `@NotNull` stays meaningful, so a malformed seed file would NPE in the log
   call itself. Treat null sections as the same startup failure.
6. `log.info("Loaded case {} with {} sections", doc.caseId(), doc.sections().size());`

Throwing from `ApplicationRunner.run` propagates out of `SpringApplication.run`, closes the
context and exits non-zero — which is the requested "must not start silently with no data".

### The startup log line you asked to see

Rendered from Boot 4.1's actual `CONSOLE_LOG_PATTERN` (pulled from
`org/springframework/boot/logging/logback/defaults.xml` in `spring-boot-4.1.0.jar`), with
`spring.application.name=cases` from `application.properties` supplying the `[cases]` segment,
and `sections.size() == 4` confirmed against the real file (`patient`, `suspect_drug`,
`adverse_event`, `reporter`):

```
2026-08-16T22:30:12.345+05:30  INFO 41287 --- [cases] [           main] com.pv.cases.config.StartupDataLoader    : Loaded case PV-2026-0451 with 4 sections
```

Timestamp and PID vary. The logger name is 37 chars, so `%-40.40logger{39}` prints it in full
padded with 3 trailing spaces — it will line up one column left of the familiar
`com.pv.cases.CasesApplication` lines around it.

## Tests (per your decision: store + startup)

- `backend/src/test/java/com/pv/cases/repository/InMemoryCaseStoreTests.java` — plain JUnit 5,
  no Spring context: `findCase` miss → `Optional.empty()`; `findQueriesByCaseId` miss → empty,
  non-null; `saveQuery` grouping by case; `queryCount()` summing across two cases; `caseCount()`.
- `backend/src/test/java/com/pv/cases/config/StartupDataLoaderTests.java` — `@SpringBootTest`
  asserting `caseCount() == 1` and `findCase("PV-2026-0451")` present with 4 sections. This is
  what actually proves the `ObjectMapper` injection resolves against Boot 4's `JsonMapper` bean.

JUnit 5 and AssertJ are already available transitively via `spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test`
→ `spring-boot-starter-test`; no `pom.xml` change needed.

**Side effect worth knowing:** `@SpringBootTest` invokes `ApplicationRunner` beans, so the
existing `CasesApplicationTests.contextLoads()` will start exercising `StartupDataLoader` too.
That is desirable here — a broken seed file becomes a build failure — but it does mean
`contextLoads()` is no longer a pure smoke test.

## Verification

1. `cd backend && mvn compile` — the real check on the `tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper`
   import and the `IOException | JacksonException` catch.
2. `mvn test` — runs all three test classes.
3. `mvn spring-boot:run` — confirm the log line above appears, and that it is emitted *after*
   the `Started CasesApplication` line (runners fire last).
4. Negative check: temporarily rename `case_v1.json` and confirm startup fails with the
   `IllegalStateException` message rather than booting empty.

Note: `maven-surefire-plugin` is not in the local `~/.m2` cache, so step 2 needs network on its
first run. Steps 1 and 3 resolve entirely offline.

content.text:
Both files plus the two test classes are in place and verified end-to-end.

## The log line — measured, not predicted

I booted the app (random port, then shut it down) rather than leaving you to check it:

```
2026-08-16T22:31:01.971+05:30  INFO 14216 --- [cases] [           main] com.pv.cases.CasesApplication            : Started CasesApplication in 0.501 seconds (process running for 0.607)
2026-08-16T22:31:01.999+05:30  INFO 14216 --- [cases] [           main] com.pv.cases.config.StartupDataLoader    : Loaded case PV-2026-0451 with 4 sections
```

Character-for-character what the plan projected, including the 3-space logger padding and the `[cases]` segment from `spring.application.name`. It lands after `Started CasesApplication`, as runners do.

## Verification

`mvn test` — **11 tests, 0 failures**: 7 store, 3 startup, plus the pre-existing `contextLoads()`. The `@SpringBootTest` passing is the real proof that `ObjectMapper` resolves against Boot 4's `JsonMapper` bean.

The three failure paths aren't reachable from the test suite, so I drove them through a standalone harness with doctored classpaths:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Resource absent | `/case_v1.json not found on the classpath; the case store would start empty` |
| Truncated JSON | `Failed to read seed case from /case_v1.json`, cause `UnexpectedEndOfInputException` |
| `case_id` mismatch | `Expected seed case PV-2026-0451 but /case_v1.json declares PV-9999-0001` |

All three leave the store empty and abort startup.

## Notes on the code

`saveQuery` uses `computeIfAbsent(...).add(...)` with **`CopyOnWriteArrayList`** values — the `ConcurrentHashMap` only protects the map, so a plain `ArrayList` would still corrupt under two concurrent saves for the same case. `findQueriesByCaseId` returns `List.copyOf(...)`; there's a test asserting the returned list rejects mutation and that stored state is unaffected.

`StartupDataLoader` catches `IOException | JacksonException` — the first reachable only from the try-with-resources `close()`, the second unchecked in Jackson 3. It also rejects a null `sections` before logging, since `CaseDocument` deliberately preserves null there and `.size()` would otherwise NPE inside the log call.

Two things I left alone, both flagged earlier and still true: `backend/target/` is tracked in git (its churn is in every diff — I filtered it out of the status above), and `backend/.mvn/wrapper/` is missing so `./mvnw` fails. Say the word and I'll fix both before the service layer.

Repository and startup layers are done and tested. Now build the merge service.

Create backend/src/main/java/com/pv/cases/service/MergeService.java

Method signature: 
public MergedCase merge(CaseDocument stored, CaseDocument followUp)

Merge logic — walk every section and field:

For each field key across the UNION of stored and followUp sections:
- Present in BOTH, value identical → MergedField with status: UNCHANGED
  (silently refresh confidence and source from followUp)
- Present in BOTH, value differs → MergedField with status: OVERRIDDEN
  previousValue = the full stored FieldValue (value + confidence + source)
  take confidence and source from followUp
- Present in followUp only → MergedField with status: NEW
- Present in stored only → MergedField with status: RETAINED
  keep stored value, confidence, source

Section-level rule: if a section exists in stored but not in followUp,
retain ALL its fields. If a section is new in followUp, mark ALL 
its fields as NEW.

Build MergeSummary by counting statuses across all fields after merging.

MergedCase fields to populate:
- caseId from stored
- version = stored.version() + 1
- baseVersion = stored.version()
- incomingVersion = followUp.version()
- caseClassification from followUp (reviewer may have updated it)
- mergedAt = Instant.now()
- sourceDocuments = merge both lists, stored first, deduped, insertion order preserved
- sections = merged map result
- summary = computed MergeSummary
- missingFields = followUp.missingFields() (nullable, pass through as-is)

Then write these unit tests in
backend/src/test/java/com/pv/cases/service/MergeServiceTest.java

Tests to cover:
1. unchangedField_sameValue_statusUnchanged
   - confidence and source are refreshed from followUp even when status=UNCHANGED
2. overriddenField_differentValue_previousValueIsFullStoredFieldValue
   - check previousValue has stored value, confidence, source
3. newField_onlyInFollowUp_statusNew
4. retainedField_onlyInStored_statusRetained
5. retainedSection_sectionMissingFromFollowUp_allFieldsRetained
6. newSection_sectionOnlyInFollowUp_allFieldsNew
7. missingFields_nullInFollowUp_nullInMergedCase
8. missingFields_presentInFollowUp_passedThrough
9. mergeSummary_countsAreCorrect_acrossAllStatuses
10. caseClassification_takenFromFollowUp_notStored

Use JUnit 5 and AssertJ. MergeService has no Spring annotations —

Done. `mvn test`: **23 tests, 0 failures** — 12 in `MergeServiceTest`, the rest unchanged.

## End-to-end against the real seed case

I merged a realistic follow-up (age corrected, event escalated to rhabdomyolysis, a new `lab_results` section, `reporter` absent) into `case_v1.json`:

```
sections in order: [patient, suspect_drug, adverse_event, reporter, lab_results]

  patient        age              overridden  "63"             conf=0.96   was "62" conf=0.91 @ p.2 §1
  patient        initials         unchanged   "M.K."           conf=0.99
  patient        weight_kg        retained    "78"             conf=0.85
  adverse_event  onset_date       unchanged   "2026-03-12"     conf=0.88
  adverse_event  seriousness      overridden  "Serious"        conf=0.94   was "Non-serious" conf=0.79 @ p.5 §1
  reporter       country          retained    "India"          conf=0.99
  lab_results    creatine_kinase  new         "8200 U/L"       conf=0.91

summary: {"unchanged":3,"overridden":4,"new":1,"retained":7}  total=15
classification: non-significant -> significant
sourceDocuments: [initial_report_PV-2026-0451.pdf, followup_PV-2026-0451.pdf]
```

`onset_date` is the rule you asked for working in the wild: same value, confidence refreshed 0.72 → 0.88, still `unchanged`. Section ordering puts the new section last, so a reviewer's familiar layout is stable.

## Implementation notes

The section-level rules aren't special-cased — a section only in `stored` yields fields that are all "stored only" and therefore all `RETAINED`, and a section only in the follow-up yields all `NEW`. The field-level union produces both outcomes for free, which is why tests 5 and 6 pass against the same code path as 3 and 4.

Null `sections` (which `CaseDocument` permits) are treated as empty rather than throwing, so a malformed follow-up degrades to "everything retained" instead of a 500.

I added two tests beyond your ten, since nothing else covered them: `mergedCaseHeader_versionsAndSourceDocumentsArePopulated` (the version arithmetic) and `sourceDocuments_sameDocumentOnBothSides_deduped` (the dedupe rule).

## One thing to decide before `CaseService`

Your spec said `sourceDocuments = merge both lists`, but `CaseDocument` has a **single** `sourceDocument` string — only `MergedCase` has the list. I implemented the only coherent reading: combine the two documents' single references, stored first, deduped.

That works perfectly for the first merge and then hits a wall. `merge()` takes two `CaseDocument`s and returns a `MergedCase`, so to merge a *second* follow-up, `CaseService` has to convert the stored `MergedCase` back into a `CaseDocument` — which collapses `sourceDocuments` (a list) into `sourceDocument` (one string) and drops the original report from the provenance chain. Three ways out, roughly in order of how much I'd recommend them:

1. Give `CaseDocument` a `sourceDocuments` list alongside the singular field, populated on merge-back.
2. Have the store keep `MergedCase` as the canonical stored type and overload `merge(MergedCase, CaseDocument)`.
3. Track provenance in the store rather than on the document.

Nothing is blocked right now — single-follow-up merges are correct and tested. It just needs an answer when we wire up `CaseService`.

```

```

Private nested records serialize fine under Jackson 3, so the bodies stayed private as you asked. The 500 handler logs the full stack trace before returning, and there's a test asserting the leaked-secret string in the cause never reaches the response body.

**I added a 4th file** — `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest.java` — which you didn't ask for. It drives the advice through `MockMvc` with a throwaway controller, so it covers handler resolution and message conversion rather than just the methods in isolation. Easy to drop if you want this step at three files.

## Two gaps worth your attention

Both are now demonstrated by passing tests rather than just asserted.

**1. `ValidationException` has no handler, so it returns 500.** You asked for the class but specified exactly three handlers, and `ValidationException` isn't one of them — it falls through to the catch-all. Anything throwing it gets `{"error":"Internal server error"}` plus an ERROR-level stack trace, when it presumably wants a 400. A fourth handler is a five-line fix; I left it out because your "Three handlers" was explicit.

**2. The catch-all masks Spring's own 4xx as 500.** This one is more insidious. `@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)` is consulted *before* Spring's `DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver`, so it claims exceptions Spring already knows how to map:

| Request | Correct | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong HTTP verb | 405 | **500** |
| Malformed JSON body | 400 | **500** |
| Unknown path | 404 | **500** |

Once `CaseController` exists, a client sending bad JSON gets a 500 and your logs fill with ERROR stack traces for what are ordinary client mistakes. The cleanest fix is `GlobalExceptionHandler extends ResponseEntityExceptionHandler` — Spring's exceptions get their correct statuses, and your three handlers still win for their own types since they're more specific. The trade-off is that those framework errors come back as RFC 9457 `ProblemDetail` bodies rather than your `{"error": ...}` shape, unless you override the hook to reshape them.

Say which way you want both, and I'll fold it in with the controller layer.

All 11 end-to-end checks pass against the live API.

| # | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /cases/PV-2026-0451` | 200, seeded case v1 |
| 2 | `POST /cases/{id}/follow-ups` | 200, full annotated diff |
| 3 | `GET /cases/PV-2026-0451` again | 200, **v2 persisted**, annotations stripped |
| 4 | `POST /queries` | **201** + generated id/timestamp |
| 5 | `GET /queries?caseId=…` | 200, the saved query |
| 6 | `GET /queries?caseId=PV-UNKNOWN` | 200 `[]` — not 404 |
| 7 | `GET /cases/PV-NOPE` | 404 `{"error":"Case not found","case_id":"PV-NOPE"}` |
| 8 | `POST /queries` blank question | 400 `{"field":"question","message":"must not be blank"}` |
| 9 | `POST /queries` unknown case | 404 |
| 10 | Follow-up with `confidence: 1.7` | 400 |
| 11 | `GET /queries` with no `caseId` | **500** ← see below |

Check 10 is worth a look — the nested `@Valid` cascade produces a precise path into the open map:

```json
{"error":"Validation failed","details":[
  {"field":"sections[patient][age].confidence","message":"must be less than or equal to 1.0"}]}
```

**I created a 4th file you didn't list**: `config/ServiceConfig.java`, a `@Configuration` with a `@Bean MergeService`. You told me last turn that `MergeService` carries no Spring annotations, and this turn that `CaseController` injects it — without a bean definition the context fails to start. Registering it externally satisfies both constraints and keeps `new MergeService()` working in `MergeServiceTest`.

I used the existing `Query.create(...)` factory rather than inlining `UUID.randomUUID()` / `Instant.now()`; it does exactly what you specified.

## Three things surfaced by the live run

**1. Check 11 is a real bug now.** A missing required `@RequestParam` raises `MissingServletRequestParameterException`, which the catch-all claims before Spring can map it — so `GET /queries` returns **500** where it should return 400. This is the catch-all problem I flagged last turn, no longer hypothetical. Still unfixed because you specified exactly three handlers.

**2. `toDocument` overwrites `extracted_at` with the merge timestamp.** `MergedCase` has `mergedAt` but `CaseDocument` has `extractedAt`, so after a merge the stored case reads `"extracted_at": "2026-08-16T17:30:46Z"` — a processing time, not an extraction time. For a PV audit trail that's arguably wrong; `followUp.extractedAt()` may be the better source. Your spec didn't cover this field, so I picked the mapping that at least never lies about being stale. Easy to flip.

**3. The provenance collapse is now visible.** Check 3 shows `"source_document": "followup.pdf"` — the initial report has dropped out. `MergedCase.sourceDocuments` was `["initial_report_….pdf", "followup.pdf"]`, but `CaseDocument` holds one string, so flattening keeps only the most recent. A second follow-up would report `["followup.pdf", "followup2.pdf"]` and the original report is gone for good. This is the design gap I raised after the merge service, now concrete — worth fixing before anyone relies on the chain.

Also unvalidated: a follow-up whose body `case_id` disagrees with the path `{caseId}` is silently accepted, and the merge keeps the stored id. That's the natural home for `ValidationException`, which currently has no caller and no handler.

**What was item 4?** Your message ends at a bare `4.` — nothing followed it.

`HealthController.java` created. No new tests added; the existing 29 still pass.

```
GET /health   HTTP 200  {"status":"UP","cases_loaded":1,"queries_count":0}
POST /queries, then GET /health again
              HTTP 200  {"status":"UP","cases_loaded":1,"queries_count":1}
```

Body shape is exactly as specified, via a private nested record with `@JsonProperty` for the two snake_case keys — same pattern as the error bodies. No `@RequestMapping` on the class since `/health` is a root path, and there's no actuator on the classpath, so nothing competes for it.

## For your manual curl pass

Endpoints now live: `GET /health`, `GET /cases/{caseId}`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/follow-ups`, `POST /queries`, `GET /queries?caseId={id}`.

Three known rough edges to expect, all previously flagged and all still open because they'd require changing something you specified:

- **`GET /queries` with no `caseId` returns 500**, not 400 — the `Exception` catch-all claims `MissingServletRequestParameterException` before Spring can map it. Same root cause turns malformed JSON into a 500 and a wrong HTTP verb into a 500 instead of 405.
- **After a follow-up, `GET /cases/{id}` shows `source_document` as only the newest file** — flattening `MergedCase` (list) into `CaseDocument` (single string) drops the initial report from the provenance chain.
- **`extracted_at` on a merged case holds the merge timestamp**, not an extraction timestamp.

Also still true: `ValidationException` has no caller and no handler, and a follow-up whose body `case_id` disagrees with the path `{caseId}` is accepted silently.

Worth knowing before you start: the store is in-memory and `POST /cases/{id}/follow-ups` mutates it, so a follow-up changes what later GETs return. Restart between passes if you want a clean slate.

input.content:
# PV Case Processing — Backend

## Overview

This service processes pharmacovigilance case data extracted from medical documents by an AI
extractor, where every field carries a value, a confidence score, and a source reference such as
`p.4 §1`. It solves the follow-up problem: when a second document arrives for a case already on
file, a reviewer needs to see exactly which fields changed, which are new, and which the extractor
simply did not find this time — so the service merges the two versions and annotates every field
with a status rather than leaving a human to diff two JSON documents by hand. On startup it loads
`case_v1.json` from the classpath into an in-memory store, which means case `PV-2026-0451` is
queryable immediately and all state is lost on restart.

## Quick Start

```bash
mvn spring-boot:run
```

Starts on port 8080. Case `PV-2026-0451` is available immediately on startup.

## API Reference

### 1. GET /cases/{caseId}

Returns the current stored state of a case. After a follow-up has been merged, this reflects the
merged result, not the original extraction.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/cases/PV-2026-0451 | jq .
```

```json
{
  "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
  "version": 1,
  "case_classification": "non-significant",
  "extracted_at": "2026-04-08T09:14:00Z",
  "source_document": "initial_report_PV-2026-0451.pdf",
  "sections": {
    "patient": {
      "initials": { "value": "M.K.", "confidence": 0.98, "source": "p.2 §1" },
      "age": { "value": "62", "confidence": 0.91, "source": "p.2 §1" },
      "sex": { "value": "Male", "confidence": 0.99, "source": "p.2 §1" },
      "weight_kg": { "value": "78", "confidence": 0.85, "source": "p.3 §2" }
    }
  }
}
```

Trimmed to the `patient` section — `suspect_drug`, `adverse_event`, and `reporter` follow the same
shape.

### 2. POST /cases/{caseId}/follow-ups

Merges a follow-up extraction into the stored case, saves the result as the new stored state, and
returns the annotated diff. Every field in the response carries a `status`; overridden fields also
carry the complete field they replaced.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/cases/PV-2026-0451/follow-ups \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
    "version": 2,
    "case_classification": "significant",
    "extracted_at": "2026-04-10T11:00:00Z",
    "source_document": "followup_report.pdf",
    "missing_fields": ["weight_kg"],
    "sections": {
      "patient": {
        "age": {"value": "63", "confidence": 0.95, "source": "p.2 §1"},
        "initials": {"value": "M.K.", "confidence": 0.98, "source": "p.2 §1"}
      },
      "adverse_event": {
        "event_term": {"value": "Myalgia", "confidence": 0.94, "source": "p.4 §1"},
        "hospitalized": {"value": "Yes", "confidence": 0.87, "source": "p.5 §2"}
      }
    }
  }' | jq .
```

```json
{
  "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
  "version": 2,
  "base_version": 1,
  "incoming_version": 2,
  "case_classification": "significant",
  "merged_at": "2026-04-10T11:04:18.211Z",
  "source_documents": [
    "initial_report_PV-2026-0451.pdf",
    "followup_report.pdf"
  ],
  "sections": {
    "patient": {
      "age": {
        "value": "63",
        "confidence": 0.95,
        "source": "p.2 §1",
        "status": "overridden",
        "previous_value": { "value": "62", "confidence": 0.91, "source": "p.2 §1" }
      },
      "initials": {
        "value": "M.K.",
        "confidence": 0.98,
        "source": "p.2 §1",
        "status": "unchanged"
      },
      "weight_kg": {
        "value": "78",
        "confidence": 0.85,
        "source": "p.3 §2",
        "status": "retained"
      }
    },
    "adverse_event": {
      "hospitalized": {
        "value": "Yes",
        "confidence": 0.87,
        "source": "p.5 §2",
        "status": "new"
      }
    }
  },
  "missing_fields": ["weight_kg"],
  "summary": { "unchanged": 2, "overridden": 1, "new": 1, "retained": 11 }
}
```

Trimmed to one field per status — `age` was overridden, `initials` was unchanged, `hospitalized` is
new, and `weight_kg` was retained because the follow-up did not mention it. The `summary` counts
cover all 15 fields in the merged case, including those omitted above.

### 3. POST /queries

Records a reviewer's question against a single field of an existing case, for human follow-up. The
case must exist; the `id` and `created_at` are generated server-side.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/queries \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
    "field_path": "patient.age",
    "question": "Is this age confirmed in the follow-up document?"
  }' | jq .
```

Returns `201 Created`:

```json
{
  "id": "4281c84c-c1f6-45fd-bc15-fb8c4af7eb7b",
  "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
  "field_path": "patient.age",
  "question": "Is this age confirmed in the follow-up document?",
  "created_at": "2026-04-10T11:06:02.615Z"
}
```

### 4. GET /queries?caseId={id}

Lists every query raised against a case, oldest first. An unknown case id returns an empty array
rather than a 404, so a reviewer UI can poll this without special-casing "no queries yet".

```bash
curl -s "http://localhost:8080/queries?caseId=PV-2026-0451" | jq .
```

```json
[
  {
    "id": "4281c84c-c1f6-45fd-bc15-fb8c4af7eb7b",
    "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
    "field_path": "patient.age",
    "question": "Is this age confirmed in the follow-up document?",
    "created_at": "2026-04-10T11:06:02.615Z"
  }
]
```

### 5. GET /health

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/health | jq .
```

```json
{
  "status": "UP",
  "cases_loaded": 1,
  "queries_count": 0
}
```

Because the store is in-memory, "the service is up" and "the service has data" are separate
questions — a `cases_loaded` of `0` is the signature of a restart that lost its state.

## Merge Behavior

| Status     | Meaning                                              |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| unchanged  | Field present in both versions, value identical      |
| overridden | Field present in both versions, value differs        |
| new        | Field present in follow-up only                      |
| retained   | Field present in stored version only                 |

Fields present in the stored version but absent from the follow-up are kept with status `retained`.
In pharmacovigilance, absence of a field in a follow-up document does not mean the field is wrong —
the AI extractor may simply not have found it in the new source. Known data is preserved until
explicitly contradicted.

Note that "differs" means value-only. If confidence or source changes but the value is the same, the
status is `unchanged` and confidence and source are silently refreshed from the follow-up. This

toolUseResult.content:
# PV Case Processing — Backend

## Overview

This service processes pharmacovigilance case data extracted from medical documents by an AI
extractor, where every field carries a value, a confidence score, and a source reference such as
`p.4 §1`. It solves the follow-up problem: when a second document arrives for a case already on
file, a reviewer needs to see exactly which fields changed, which are new, and which the extractor
simply did not find this time — so the service merges the two versions and annotates every field
with a status rather than leaving a human to diff two JSON documents by hand. On startup it loads
`case_v1.json` from the classpath into an in-memory store, which means case `PV-2026-0451` is
queryable immediately and all state is lost on restart.

## Quick Start

```bash
mvn spring-boot:run
```

Starts on port 8080. Case `PV-2026-0451` is available immediately on startup.

## API Reference

### 1. GET /cases/{caseId}

Returns the current stored state of a case. After a follow-up has been merged, this reflects the
merged result, not the original extraction.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/cases/PV-2026-0451 | jq .
```

```json
{
  "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
  "version": 1,
  "case_classification": "non-significant",
  "extracted_at": "2026-04-08T09:14:00Z",
  "source_document": "initial_report_PV-2026-0451.pdf",
  "sections": {
    "patient": {
      "initials": { "value": "M.K.", "confidence": 0.98, "source": "p.2 §1" },
      "age": { "value": "62", "confidence": 0.91, "source": "p.2 §1" },
      "sex": { "value": "Male", "confidence": 0.99, "source": "p.2 §1" },
      "weight_kg": { "value": "78", "confidence": 0.85, "source": "p.3 §2" }
    }
  }
}
```

Trimmed to the `patient` section — `suspect_drug`, `adverse_event`, and `reporter` follow the same
shape.

### 2. POST /cases/{caseId}/follow-ups

Merges a follow-up extraction into the stored case, saves the result as the new stored state, and
returns the annotated diff. Every field in the response carries a `status`; overridden fields also
carry the complete field they replaced.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/cases/PV-2026-0451/follow-ups \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
    "version": 2,
    "case_classification": "significant",
    "extracted_at": "2026-04-10T11:00:00Z",
    "source_document": "followup_report.pdf",
    "missing_fields": ["weight_kg"],
    "sections": {
      "patient": {
        "age": {"value": "63", "confidence": 0.95, "source": "p.2 §1"},
        "initials": {"value": "M.K.", "confidence": 0.98, "source": "p.2 §1"}
      },
      "adverse_event": {
        "event_term": {"value": "Myalgia", "confidence": 0.94, "source": "p.4 §1"},
        "hospitalized": {"value": "Yes", "confidence": 0.87, "source": "p.5 §2"}
      }
    }
  }' | jq .
```

```json
{
  "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
  "version": 2,
  "base_version": 1,
  "incoming_version": 2,
  "case_classification": "significant",
  "merged_at": "2026-04-10T11:04:18.211Z",
  "source_documents": [
    "initial_report_PV-2026-0451.pdf",
    "followup_report.pdf"
  ],
  "sections": {
    "patient": {
      "age": {
        "value": "63",
        "confidence": 0.95,
        "source": "p.2 §1",
        "status": "overridden",
        "previous_value": { "value": "62", "confidence": 0.91, "source": "p.2 §1" }
      },
      "initials": {
        "value": "M.K.",
        "confidence": 0.98,
        "source": "p.2 §1",
        "status": "unchanged"
      },
      "weight_kg": {
        "value": "78",
        "confidence": 0.85,
        "source": "p.3 §2",
        "status": "retained"
      }
    },
    "adverse_event": {
      "hospitalized": {
        "value": "Yes",
        "confidence": 0.87,
        "source": "p.5 §2",
        "status": "new"
      }
    }
  },
  "missing_fields": ["weight_kg"],
  "summary": { "unchanged": 2, "overridden": 1, "new": 1, "retained": 11 }
}
```

Trimmed to one field per status — `age` was overridden, `initials` was unchanged, `hospitalized` is
new, and `weight_kg` was retained because the follow-up did not mention it. The `summary` counts
cover all 15 fields in the merged case, including those omitted above.

### 3. POST /queries

Records a reviewer's question against a single field of an existing case, for human follow-up. The
case must exist; the `id` and `created_at` are generated server-side.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/queries \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
    "field_path": "patient.age",
    "question": "Is this age confirmed in the follow-up document?"
  }' | jq .
```

Returns `201 Created`:

```json
{
  "id": "4281c84c-c1f6-45fd-bc15-fb8c4af7eb7b",
  "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
  "field_path": "patient.age",
  "question": "Is this age confirmed in the follow-up document?",
  "created_at": "2026-04-10T11:06:02.615Z"
}
```

### 4. GET /queries?caseId={id}

Lists every query raised against a case, oldest first. An unknown case id returns an empty array
rather than a 404, so a reviewer UI can poll this without special-casing "no queries yet".

```bash
curl -s "http://localhost:8080/queries?caseId=PV-2026-0451" | jq .
```

```json
[
  {
    "id": "4281c84c-c1f6-45fd-bc15-fb8c4af7eb7b",
    "case_id": "PV-2026-0451",
    "field_path": "patient.age",
    "question": "Is this age confirmed in the follow-up document?",
    "created_at": "2026-04-10T11:06:02.615Z"
  }
]
```

### 5. GET /health

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8080/health | jq .
```

```json
{
  "status": "UP",
  "cases_loaded": 1,
  "queries_count": 0
}
```

Because the store is in-memory, "the service is up" and "the service has data" are separate
questions — a `cases_loaded` of `0` is the signature of a restart that lost its state.

## Merge Behavior

| Status     | Meaning                                              |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| unchanged  | Field present in both versions, value identical      |
| overridden | Field present in both versions, value differs        |
| new        | Field present in follow-up only                      |
| retained   | Field present in stored version only                 |

Fields present in the stored version but absent from the follow-up are kept with status `retained`.
In pharmacovigilance, absence of a field in a follow-up document does not mean the field is wrong —
the AI extractor may simply not have found it in the new source. Known data is preserved until
explicitly contradicted.

Note that "differs" means value-only. If confidence or source changes but the value is the same, the
status is `unchanged` and confidence and source are silently refreshed from the follow-up. This
prevents spurious `overridden` flags from re-extraction noise — a confidence drifting from 0.94 to
0.95 is not a change a reviewer needs to adjudicate.

The same rules apply at the section level, as a consequence rather than a special case. A section
present only in the stored case contributes fields that are all `retained`; a section introduced by
the follow-up contributes fields that are all `new`.

## Running Tests

```bash
mvn test
```

- `MergeService`: 12 tests
- `GlobalExceptionHandler`: 6 tests
- Application context smoke test: 1 test

# Stage 1: Build the jar using full JDK
# Stage 2: Run with minimal JRE image, non-root user

RUN chown appuser:appgroup app.jar

USER appuser
EXPOSE 8080

ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]

content.text:
`Dockerfile` created at the repo root, following your spec with **one deviation**, which I want to be upfront about.

## The builder base image had to change

`eclipse-temurin` ships a JDK only — no build tooling. I pulled both image configs from the registry to confirm rather than assume:

```
eclipse-temurin:17.0.10_7-jdk-alpine     PATH=/opt/java/openjdk/bin:/usr/local/sbin:...   (no MAVEN_HOME)
maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-17-alpine    PATH=...same...   MAVEN_HOME=/usr/share/maven
```

So `RUN mvn dependency:go-offline -B` in the Temurin JDK image fails with `mvn: not found`, and the build never reaches stage 2. Your `./mvnw` isn't an escape hatch either — `backend/.mvn/wrapper/` is missing from the repo, so the wrapper is broken (I flagged this a few steps back).

I switched stage 1 to `maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-17-alpine`: same Temurin 17 JDK, same Alpine, with Maven present. **Everything else is exactly as you specified** — the four-step layer order, the `-B` flags, the runtime stage's pinned `eclipse-temurin:17.0.10_7-jre-alpine`, the non-root user, `EXPOSE 8080`, the entrypoint. No `COPY . .` anywhere.

If you'd rather keep the exact Temurin builder pin, the alternative is `RUN apk add --no-cache maven` after the `FROM` — one extra line, but it pulls Alpine's own OpenJDK as a dependency and you lose the Maven version pin.

## What I verified without a daemon

Docker's daemon isn't running here (`/var/run/docker.sock` absent), so I could not `docker build`. Everything checkable another way, I checked:

- Both `17.0.10_7-jdk-alpine` and `17.0.10_7-jre-alpine` exist on Docker Hub — your tags were right.
- Spring Boot 4.1 and Framework 7 are compiled to bytecode major 61 = Java 17, so the JDK 17 baseline is sound.
- `COPY backend/pom.xml` and `COPY backend/src` both resolve from a repo-root build context.
- Ran `mvn package -DskipTests -B` for real: succeeds, and `target/` gets exactly one `*.jar` match — `cases-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar`, since `.jar.original` doesn't match the glob. So the `COPY --from=builder` line is unambiguous.
- Ran the packaged jar exactly as `ENTRYPOINT` does — it boots, seeds the case, and serves: `{"status":"UP","cases_loaded":1,"queries_count":0}`.

## One thing to expect on your Mac

Both `eclipse-temurin:17.0.10_7-*-alpine` tags are **amd64-only**. On Apple Silicon, `docker build` will either need `--platform linux/amd64` and run under emulation, or fail outright depending on your Docker version. If you want a native arm64 image, the non-alpine `eclipse-temurin:17-jre` is multi-arch — at the cost of a larger runtime layer and dropping your exact patch pin.

I did not add a `.dockerignore`; with explicit `COPY backend/pom.xml` and `COPY backend/src`, nothing stray can enter the context, and `backend/target/` is a sibling of `src` so it's never copied.

version: '3.8'

services:
  pv-cases:
    # Build context is the repository root, not backend/, because the Dockerfile
    # copies backend/pom.xml and backend/src separately to keep the dependency
    # layer cacheable. A backend/ context could not see those paths.
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    container_name: pv-cases
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

    # JVM flags live in the environment rather than baked into an image layer,
    # so heap size can be changed at `docker compose up` time without a rebuild.
    # Note: this only takes effect if the image entrypoint expands $JAVA_OPTS.
    # The current ENTRYPOINT is exec form (["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]), which
    # performs no shell expansion, so this value is inert as things stand —
    # either switch the entrypoint to shell form or use JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS,
    # which the JVM reads from the environment on its own.
    environment:
      - JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx512m

    # wget rather than curl: it is guaranteed present in the runtime image, and
    # --spider issues the request without writing the body to disk, so the check
    # costs nothing but the round trip. /health also reports store contents, so
    # an "up but empty" container is still reported healthy — liveness only.
    #
    # start_period of 40s covers JVM startup: container start, class loading,
    # Spring context refresh and the case seeding all happen before the first
    # port bind. Failures during this window are not counted against `retries`,
    # so a slow cold start on a loaded host cannot mark the service unhealthy.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 40s

    # Restarts the container after a crash or a host/daemon reboot, but stays
    # down after an explicit `docker compose stop` or `down` — so recovery is
    # automatic while a deliberate shutdown is respected.
    restart: unless-stopped

content.text:
`docker-compose.yml` created at the repo root and verified end-to-end against a real `docker compose up --build`.

```
NAME       COMMAND               STATUS                   PORTS
pv-cases   "java -jar app.jar"   Up 5 seconds (healthy)   0.0.0.0:8080->8080/tcp

healthcheck log:   exit=0
/health:           {"status":"UP","cases_loaded":1,"queries_count":0}  HTTP 200
running as user:   uid=999(appuser) gid=999(appgroup)
restart policy:    unless-stopped
```

Healthy at **t+6s** — the container reports healthy well inside the 40s start period, and the non-root user carries through from the Dockerfile.

## Your `wget` reasoning was right, the premise wasn't

The Dockerfile is now on `eclipse-temurin:17-jre`, which is **Ubuntu 26.04, not Alpine** — and it ships *both*:

```
/usr/bin/wget
/usr/bin/curl
```

So `wget` works (exit code 0, confirmed above) and needs no change. Just don't rely on "curl isn't installed" as a constraint going forward — on this base it is.

## One thing in your spec is inert

`JAVA_OPTS` reaches the container but never reaches the JVM:

```
env in container: -Xmx512m
pid 1 cmdline:    java -jar app.jar
```

The exec-form `ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]` runs no shell, so `$JAVA_OPTS` is never expanded — the heap cap is not applied. That defeats the stated purpose of "override at runtime without rebuilding". Two fixes:

- **`JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` instead of `JAVA_OPTS`** — the JVM reads it from the environment by itself. No Dockerfile change, one word in compose.
- **Shell-form entrypoint** — `ENTRYPOINT ["sh", "-c", "exec java $JAVA_OPTS -jar app.jar"]`. Keeps the variable name; needs `exec` so the JVM stays PID 1 and receives signals.

I left it as `JAVA_OPTS` per your spec and documented the caveat in a comment in the file. Say which fix you want and I'll apply it.

Also worth noting: `version: '3.8'` is obsolete under Compose v2 and produces a warning on every command — `the attribute 'version' is obsolete, it will be ignored`. Harmless, but it'll appear in every `up`, `ps`, and `config`. Deleting that one line silences it; I kept it because you specified it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# ops/run.sh — single entrypoint for operational tasks.
#
# Run `ops/run.sh --help` for the command list.

set -euo pipefail

# Resolve the repository root from this script's own location, then work from
# there. docker-compose.yml lives at the root while this script lives in ops/,
# so without this the commands would only work when invoked from one specific
# directory — the last thing anyone wants to discover at 2am.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

HEALTH_URL="http://localhost:8080/health"
HEALTH_ATTEMPTS=10
HEALTH_INTERVAL=3

log() { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*" >&2; }

usage() {
	cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ops/run.sh <command>

Commands:
  build   Build the Docker image
  start   Start the service and wait for healthy status
  stop    Stop the service
  test    Run unit tests and verify service health
  logs    Tail service logs
  clean   Remove containers, volumes, and local images
EOF
}

# Fail fast with an actionable message rather than letting the underlying tool
# emit something cryptic.
require_docker() {
	if ! docker info > /dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "[ERROR] Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop first." >&2
		exit 1
	fi
}

require_cmd() {
	if ! command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "[ERROR] Required command not found: $1" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
}

# Single health probe. Separated so `start` and `test` cannot drift apart in
# what they consider a healthy service.
health_ok() {
	curl -sf -o /dev/null "${HEALTH_URL}"
}

cmd_build() {
	require_docker
	log "Building Docker image..."
	docker-compose build
	log "Build complete"
}

cmd_start() {
	require_docker
	require_cmd curl

	log "Starting service..."
	docker-compose up -d

	log "Waiting for ${HEALTH_URL} (up to $((HEALTH_ATTEMPTS * HEALTH_INTERVAL))s)..."
	attempt=1
	while [ "${attempt}" -le "${HEALTH_ATTEMPTS}" ]; do
		if health_ok; then
			log "Service is UP"
			return 0
		fi
		log "  attempt ${attempt}/${HEALTH_ATTEMPTS} - not ready yet"
		if [ "${attempt}" -lt "${HEALTH_ATTEMPTS}" ]; then
			sleep "${HEALTH_INTERVAL}"
		fi
		attempt=$((attempt + 1))
	done

	log "Service failed to start - check logs with: ops/run.sh logs"
	return 1
}

cmd_stop() {
	require_docker
	log "Stopping service..."
	docker-compose down
	log "Service stopped"
}

# Both parts must pass. Unit tests run against the working tree and need no
# container; the health check needs a running service.
cmd_test() {
	require_cmd mvn
	require_cmd curl

	log "Running unit tests..."
	if ! mvn test -f backend/pom.xml; then
		log "Unit tests failed"
		return 1
	fi
	log "Unit tests passed"

	log "Checking service health..."
	if ! health_ok; then
		log "Service is not running - start it first with: ops/run.sh start"
		return 1
	fi
	log "Service health check passed"
}

cmd_logs() {
	require_docker
	log "Tailing service logs (Ctrl-C to stop)..."
	docker-compose logs -f
}

cmd_clean() {
	require_docker
	log "Removing containers, volumes, and local images..."
	docker-compose down -v --rmi local
	log "Cleaned up containers, volumes, and local images"
}

main() {
	if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
		usage >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	subcommand="$1"

	case "${subcommand}" in
		--help | -h | help)
			usage
			exit 0
			;;
	esac

	cd -- "${REPO_ROOT}"

	case "${subcommand}" in
		build) cmd_build ;;
		start) cmd_start ;;
		stop) cmd_stop ;;
		test) cmd_test ;;
		logs) cmd_logs ;;
		clean) cmd_clean ;;
		*)
			echo "Unknown command: ${subcommand}" >&2
			usage >&2
			exit 1
			;;
	esac
}

main "$@"

`bash -n` is clean and a scan for unquoted expansions found none. I rebuilt the image at the end so your environment is as I found it — `clean` genuinely removed it, and step 10 put it back.

## Two things I added beyond the spec

**Repo-root resolution.** The script derives its own location via `BASH_SOURCE` and `cd`s to the repo root before running anything. Without it, `docker-compose` wouldn't find `docker-compose.yml` and `mvn -f backend/pom.xml` wouldn't resolve unless you happened to be standing in the repo root — a footgun precisely when you're least able to debug it. Verified by running `start` from `/tmp`: it worked.

**A `require_cmd` guard** for `mvn` and `curl`, so a missing tool gives `[ERROR] Required command not found: mvn` instead of a raw shell error. Note `test` deliberately does *not* call `require_docker` — it runs Maven against the working tree and only probes health over HTTP, so it needs no daemon, matching your spec.

I also factored the health probe into one `health_ok` function shared by `start` and `test`, so the two can't drift on what "healthy" means.

## Worth knowing

`docker-compose` here is a shim over Compose **v5.3.1** — it works, which is why I used your syntax verbatim. But on a Linux host with only the v2 plugin, `docker-compose` may not exist while `docker compose` does. If this script will ever run somewhere other than your Mac, a two-line detection at the top would make it portable:

```bash
if command -v docker-compose > /dev/null 2>&1; then COMPOSE=(docker-compose); else COMPOSE=(docker compose); fi
```

then `"${COMPOSE[@]}" build`. Say the word and I'll fold it in.

Bash here is **3.2.57** (Apple's system bash), so I kept to 3.2-compatible constructs throughout — no associative arrays, no `mapfile`. It'll run identically on newer bash.

One inherited caveat: `start` polls `/health` directly rather than reading the container's healthcheck status, so it reports UP as soon as the endpoint answers — typically ~3s, well before Docker flips the container to `healthy` (it showed `health: starting` at that moment). That's the behaviour you specified and it's the more useful signal for a human waiting at a terminal; just don't read "Service is UP" as "Docker considers it healthy".

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# ops/backup.sh — snapshot stored cases to a timestamped JSON array.
#
# Non-interactive and safe to run from cron. Environment overrides:
#   BASE_URL     service base URL      (default http://localhost:8080)
#   BACKUP_DIR   output directory      (default <repo>/backups)

set -euo pipefail

# Resolve the repository root from this script's own location and work from
# there, so a relative BACKUP_DIR always lands in the same place. Cron runs with
# the invoking user's home as the working directory, not the repo.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
cd -- "${REPO_ROOT}"

BASE_URL="${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8080}"
CASE_IDS=("PV-2026-0451")   # extend this list for more cases
BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR:-backups}"
TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
OUTFILE="${BACKUP_DIR}/backup_${TIMESTAMP}.json"

log() { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*" >&2; }

require_cmd() {
	if ! command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
		log "[ERROR] Required command not found: $1"
		exit 1
	fi
}

# Scratch files are removed on every exit path, so an aborted run leaves no
# debris and — crucially — no half-written file that looks like a real backup.
TMPFILE=""
cleanup() {
	if [ -n "${TMPFILE}" ]; then
		rm -f -- "${TMPFILE}" "${TMPFILE}.json"
	fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

main() {
	log "Starting backup from ${BASE_URL}"

	require_cmd curl
	require_cmd jq

	# Guard the empty case: under `set -u`, bash 3.2 treats "${CASE_IDS[@]}" on
	# an empty array as an unbound variable, which would abort with a message
	# that says nothing about the real problem.
	if [ "${#CASE_IDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
		log "[ERROR] CASE_IDS is empty - nothing to back up"
		exit 1
	fi

	if ! curl -sf -o /dev/null "${BASE_URL}/health"; then
		log "[ERROR] Service is not reachable at ${BASE_URL} - start it with: ops/run.sh start"
		exit 1
	fi

	mkdir -p -- "${BACKUP_DIR}"

	# Staged inside BACKUP_DIR rather than /tmp so the final mv is a same
	# filesystem rename, and therefore atomic: readers see either no file or a
	# complete one, never a partial write.
	TMPFILE="$(mktemp "${BACKUP_DIR}/.backup_${TIMESTAMP}.XXXXXX")"

	for case_id in "${CASE_IDS[@]}"; do
		log "Fetching ${case_id}"
		if ! curl -sf "${BASE_URL}/cases/${case_id}" >> "${TMPFILE}"; then
			log "[ERROR] Failed to fetch ${case_id} - aborting without writing a backup"
			exit 1
		fi
		printf '\n' >> "${TMPFILE}"
	done

	# jq -s slurps the concatenated objects into one array. It also parses every
	# response, so a 200 carrying malformed JSON fails here rather than producing
	# a backup that only reveals itself as broken during a restore.
	if ! jq -s '.' "${TMPFILE}" > "${TMPFILE}.json"; then
		log "[ERROR] Response was not valid JSON - aborting without writing a backup"
		exit 1
	fi

	mv -- "${TMPFILE}.json" "${OUTFILE}"

	log "Backed up ${#CASE_IDS[@]} case(s)"
	log "Backup written to ${OUTFILE}"
	exit 0
}

main "$@"

`ops/backup.sh` created and executable. `bash -n` clean, no unquoted expansions.

Docker's daemon had stopped again, so I ran the packaged jar on :8080 instead — the script only speaks HTTP, so it's an equivalent target.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Service down | `[ERROR] Service is not reachable…` → **exit 1**, no `backups/` created |
| Happy path | `Backup written to backups/backup_20260817_084613.json` → **exit 0** |
| File shape | `type=array length=1`, case intact with confidence + `p.2 §1` source |
| Temp debris | 0 leftover files |
| Run from `/tmp` | Same output path — repo-root resolution works |
| `BASE_URL=…:9999` | → **exit 1** |
| Nonexistent case ID | `aborting without writing a backup` → **exit 1**, **0 files written** |

## One real flaw, which my own test tripped

`TIMESTAMP` has one-second resolution, and `mv` overwrites without complaint. Steps 2 and 5 of my test both ran inside the same second, produced the identical filename `backup_20260817_084613.json`, and the second run **silently destroyed the first** — the directory ended with one file, not two.

Under cron this is near-impossible (minute granularity at worst). But for a *backup* script, silent overwrite is the wrong failure mode. One-line fix, your call:

```bash
mv -n -- "${TMPFILE}.json" "${OUTFILE}"   # refuse to clobber
```
…or add `$$` to the filename. I left your `date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S` format exactly as specified.

## What the backup does not contain

It captures **cases only**. The store also holds reviewer queries (`GET /queries?caseId=…`), and those are not in the snapshot — restoring from one of these files would bring back case data with every query lost. Since queries are the human-authored part of the system, that's arguably the more valuable half. Your `CASE_IDS` spec covers only cases, so I built exactly that; adding a parallel query fetch is straightforward if you want it.

## Beyond your spec

- **Repo-root resolution** and `cd`, so relative `BACKUP_DIR` is deterministic under cron, where the working directory is the invoking user's home.
- **Atomic publish**: responses are staged in a `mktemp` file *inside* `BACKUP_DIR` (same filesystem, so the final `mv` is a true rename) and an `EXIT` trap removes scratch files. A killed run can never leave a truncated file that looks like a valid backup. Verified: the failed-case-ID run left zero files and zero debris.
- **`jq -s` doubles as validation** — a 200 carrying malformed JSON fails at backup time rather than at restore time.
- **`require_cmd` for `curl`/`jq`** and an empty-`CASE_IDS` guard, since bash 3.2 under `set -u` treats `"${CASE_IDS[@]}"` on an empty array as an unbound variable and would abort with a message that explains nothing.
- **`BACKUP_DIR` made overridable** via `${BACKUP_DIR:-backups}`, matching the `BASE_URL` idiom you used, so cron can target a mounted volume.

Two housekeeping notes: I removed the `backups/` directory my test created, and `backups/` will show up untracked once you run this for real — probably wants a `.gitignore` entry. Step 7 used a modified *copy* in scratch; your `ops/backup.sh` still lists only `PV-2026-0451`.
